name: Altair Feko
version_reference: 2025.1 (verified against a 2026.1 installation and the online reference)
description: Feko is Altair's computational electromagnetics (CEM) suite, best known for hybridising several solvers in one model: the Method of Moments (MoM) with the Multilevel Fast Multipole Method (MLFMM) for electrically large structures, the Finite Element Method (FEM) for inhomogeneous dielectrics, the Finite Difference Time Domain (FDTD) method, and the asymptotic Physical Optics (PO, large-element PO), Ray Launching Geometrical Optics (RL-GO) and Uniform Theory of Diffraction (UTD) solvers for electrically huge platforms. Its strengths are antenna design, antenna placement and co-site analysis on vehicles, aircraft, ships and satellites, radar cross section (RCS), EMC/EMI and cable coupling, radomes, bio-electromagnetics (SAR), periodic structures and metamaterials, and characteristic mode analysis (CMA); with WinProp it extends to wave propagation and radio network planning. The workflow has three tools: CADFEKO builds or imports geometry, meshes it, sets media, ports, sources, loads, frequencies and result requests, and runs the solver; EDITFEKO is the text 'card' front end (.pre files with variables and loops) for the same solver; POSTFEKO visualises far fields, near fields, currents, S-parameters, impedances, SAR and CMA data and exports them. OPTFEKO drives optimisation over model variables; adaptive frequency sampling (continuous frequency ranges) runs inside the solver launcher. Feko is part of Altair HyperWorks and licensed with Altair Units.

automation.summary: Three headless entry points. (1) The runfeko command (syntax: runfeko FILENAME [OPTIONS], FILENAME = .cfx, .pre, .fek or .nfp) pre-processes with cadfeko_batch/PREFEKO as needed and solves without any GUI, writing the text .out file, the binary .bof result file and every requested export (.ffe far fields, .efe/.hfe near fields, Touchstone .sNp); -np N runs the MPI-parallel solver. It prints a banner 'Altair Feko - RUNFEKO Version <version>' on every invocation; note that --version/--help must not be the first argument (that is taken as the file name, ERROR 20006) and that bare runfeko prints the usage (exit code 2). (2) CADFEKO and POSTFEKO embed Lua with a complete object API (cf.* in CADFEKO, pf.* in POSTFEKO). Scripts run from the built-in script editor, or headless with 'cadfeko --non-interactive --run-script build.lua' and 'postfeko --non-interactive --run-script extract.lua' (the documented command line form; there is no postfeko_batch executable and cadfeko_batch does not accept --run-script). The installed cf API is the 2019-format object tree (cf.GetApplication(), project.Geometry, project.Media, project.SolutionConfigurations, project.Launcher); the online API reference documents the newer form (cf.Application.GetInstance(), project.Contents.Geometry, project.Definitions.Media) whose method names are otherwise the same. Every GUI action can be recorded as Lua, which is the fastest way to discover the exact call for any dialog. (3) cadfeko_batch model.cfx is a batch processor for .cfx files (change model variables with -#VAR=VALUE, --force-mesh, --cable-seed, --file-info) that regenerates the .cfm/.pre; a .pre file is plain text, so any program can generate cards and call prefeko/runfeko, and the .out file and the export files are plain text too, so results can be parsed with ordinary scripts.

cli.description: Pre-process (cadfeko_batch + PREFEKO if the .cfm/.fek are missing or older) and solve a CADFEKO model headless; writes model.out, model.bof and the requested export files next to it.
Same, with 8 MPI processes for the parallel solver (MoM, MLFMM, FEM, FDTD all run in parallel); -np all uses every process listed in the machines file.
Solve an EDITFEKO card file (PREFEKO converts it to model.fek first). A continuous (adaptive) frequency range is handled inside this run; there is no separate adaptfeko executable.

Without arguments prints the RUNFEKO banner (with the installed version) and the usage, exit code 2; the cheapest check that the installation works. Do not pass --version or --help as the first argument (it is treated as a file name and fails with ERROR 20006).
Only pre-process: expand variables/loops and write model.fek without solving; -#var=value overrides a variable, --print-variables lists all variables, --ignore-errors continues after card errors.

Batch-process a CADFEKO model without the GUI: set model variables (-#VAR=VALUE), force re-meshing, set --cable-seed, or print --file-info[=xml]; it regenerates the .cfm and .pre. Options: -h/--help, --version, --run-from-gui, --file-info, -#VAR=VALUE, --cable-seed, --force-mesh (it does NOT run Lua scripts).

Execute a CADFEKO Lua script without user interaction (build geometry, mesh, save the .cfx/.cfm, optionally launch the solver with project.Launcher:RunFEKO()). The working directory is set to the script's folder; --configure-script CONFIGSTRING executes a Lua string before the script.
Execute a POSTFEKO Lua script without user interaction (open a .fek/.bof, read data sets, export CSV/images/reports).

Run an OPTFEKO optimisation defined in model.opt (created by CADFEKO's optimisation search) which repeatedly calls the solver; --restart x resumes, -r deletes interim files, --runfeko-options -np 4 passes solver options.

apis.name: CADFEKO Lua API (cf)
apis.description: Complete object model of CADFEKO: application, project (Geometry, Media, Mesher, SolutionConfigurations, SolutionSettings, Ports, Variables, NamedPoints, Workplanes, Optimisation, Cable, Importer/Exporter) and the project Launcher. Every model can be built, meshed, saved and solved from a script; the script recorder turns GUI actions into equivalent Lua. cf.Point(x, y, z) takes three numbers.
apis.example:
app = cf.GetApplication()
project = app:NewProject()
project.Variables:Add("len", "0.47*c0/3e8")
wire = project.Geometry:AddLine(cf.Point(0, 0, -0.235), cf.Point(0, 0, 0.235))
port = project.Ports:AddWirePort(wire.Wires[1])
port.Location = cf.Enums.WirePortLocationEnum.Middle
cfg = project.SolutionConfigurations[1]
src = cfg.Sources:AddVoltageSource(port)
src.Impedance = 50
cfg.Frequency.Start = 3e8
cfg.FarFields:Add3DPattern()
project.Mesher:Mesh()
app:SaveAs([[D:/work/dipole.cfx]])
result = project.Launcher:RunFEKO()
print(result.Succeeded)

apis.name: POSTFEKO Lua API (pf)
apis.description: Open solved models, walk their configurations and requests (FarFields, NearFields, Excitations, Loads, SParameters, Power, SurfaceCurrents, WireCurrents, SAR, CharacteristicModes, ReceivingAntennas, TRCoefficients, ErrorEstimates), obtain DataSet objects with axes and quantities, do math on them, plot to graphs/3D views and export data, images, animations and reports.
apis.example:
app = pf.GetApplication()
app:OpenFile([[D:/work/dipole.fek]])
cfg = app.Models[1].Configurations[1]
ds = cfg.FarFields[1]:GetDataSet()
print(ds)  -- axes Frequency/Theta/Phi, quantities EFieldTheta, EFieldPhi, DirectivityFactor, GainFactor, RealisedGainFactor
g = ds[1][1][1].GainFactor
print(10*math.log10(g), "dBi at theta=0")
z = cfg.Excitations[1]:GetDataSet()[1].Impedance
print(z.re, z.im)
cfg.FarFields[1]:ExportData([[D:/work/dipole_ff]], pf.Enums.FarFieldsExportTypeEnum.Gain, 1)

apis.name: EDITFEKO cards (.pre)
apis.description: Text input: geometry cards (DP, BL, BP, BQ, BT, PM, KU, ZY, QU...), control cards (FR frequency, A1 voltage source, LS/LZ loads, FF/FE/OS/SP requests) with #variables and expressions, !!for/!!next loops, !!if/!!else/!!endif blocks and !!print statements; EG separates geometry from control cards, EN ends the file. Cards are colon-separated (DP: A : : : : : x : y : z) or column based.

apis.name: Application macros
apis.description: Lua scripts shipped with Feko (CADFEKO: Generate Antenna Array, Compare CADFEKO Models, Create Edge Port on Finite Substrate, Create Coaxial Feed; POSTFEKO: MIMO Performance Evaluation, Multiport Post-Processing, S-parameter plotter, Characteristic Mode plotter/synthesis, Interference matrix, Reciprocal configuration) plus a user macro library under FEKO_USER_HOME/applicationmacrolibrary; they are ordinary Lua files that can be copied and adapted.

file_formats.description: CADFEKO model: geometry, media, solution settings, requests (binary container; _optimum suffix after an optimisation).
CADFEKO mesh belonging to the .cfx; regenerated by cadfeko_batch; runfeko needs both.
EDITFEKO card-based input file (text); CADFEKO writes one on every save.
Solver input produced by PREFEKO/CADFEKO (mesh + control cards); what POSTFEKO opens together with the .bof.
Human-readable solver output: model summary, memory/time, warnings, source data, impedances, power, requested near/far fields, S-parameters.
Binary output file with all results for POSTFEKO.
Far-field export (theta/phi with E-field components, gain/directivity per frequency).
Near-field E and H exports at the requested points.
Currents and charges export on triangles and segments.
OPTFEKO optimisation definition (variables, goals, method) and the optimisation bookkeeping file.
POSTFEKO session (views, graphs, imported files, math scripts).
Solver intermediate files: current coefficients, MoM matrix, LU factors, right-hand sides, numerical Green's function, PO shadowing information, iterative-solver residuum (reusable between runs).
